question.question:
Use solely the fictional, scenario-specific leverage rule set out here. Before any deductions, gross Tier 1 capital stands at 510 USD million. The entire goodwill balance of 20 USD million is deducted. Deferred tax assets amount to 50 USD million, and only the portion exceeding 15 percent of gross Tier 1 capital is deducted; when the DTA do not exceed that threshold, there is no DTA deduction at all. The exposure measure is the sum of two items: on-balance-sheet assets of 7500 USD million, counted in full, and undrawn commitments of 1300 USD million, counted at 50 percent of their notional amount. The leverage ratio, expressed in percent, equals Tier 1 capital after deductions divided by the exposure measure, multiplied by 100. The required minimum ratio is 4.5 percent. The capital shortfall is the extra Tier 1 capital, in USD million, needed to lift the ratio to exactly the minimum while the exposure measure stays the same; it is 0 whenever the ratio is already at or above the minimum. Should Tier 1 capital after deductions be zero or negative, the case is invalid. Carry every value exactly. Give Tier 1 capital after deductions, the exposure measure, the leverage ratio in percent, and lastly the capital shortfall.

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `usd_million`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.
